source.title: What to Forget in Unlearning? Forget Set Curation for Language Models
source.authors: Animesh Jha; Arpandeep Khatua; Youssef Allouah; O. Koyejo

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the model, curator, metric, and value assignments are supported by the table layout.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning’s effect on targeted verbatim extraction and retention using its own curation benchmark and extraction metric; it does not test the claim’s recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper measures target-pool and retain-pool extractability after unlearning, plus QA and general validation changes. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting. Corpus-overlap and baseline extractability results are not rows because they do not apply or evaluate an unlearning intervention. The unlearning prompts in the appendix are task prompts, not instructions addressed to an AI reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether unlearning (SimNPO, UNDIAL, RMU) suppresses target verbatim extraction while preserving other content and general benchmarks. This is a new setting (copyrighted songs and books, curated forget sets) with direct results on version A's effectiveness and preservation parts. It runs no recovery attacks (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, prompting), so B–F and A's attack-resistance clause are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that forget-set curation and the unlearner must be evaluated jointly. Retrieval-derived forget sets compose unpredictably with the unlearner: the same BM25-pre set gives 10.5%, 98.2% or 32.8% suppression under SimNPO, UNDIAL or RMU. Evaluation-aware curation suppresses targets almost completely but also suppresses non-target content, with model- and algorithm-dependent capability loss. No tested configuration was selective. Recovery attacks are not studied.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates SimNPO, UNDIAL, and RMU with curated target windows and probabilistic extraction; it does not reproduce the cited recovery-attack methods or test gradient ascent, Who’s Harry Potter, or quantization/prompt recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary substantially with curator, model, and unlearning algorithm. Under retrieval curation, model size tracks suppression; with the same EA inputs, SimNPO, UNDIAL, and RMU yield different capability outcomes. RMU is especially variable across models.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported in the supplied text. The evaluation-aware curator directly uses evaluation windows and is described as a robustness test rather than a practical curator. Retrieval output sizes differ, which also changes optimizer updates. General capability results vary by benchmark and unlearner; the reported average can conceal these differences.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted the Table 1 per-model QA deltas and individual validation-benchmark deltas; Table 2 per-model benchmark/QA values; Table 3 curator-by-unlearner averages; and Appendix Table 6 results for |F|=100. The kept rows prioritize per-model target and retain extraction outcomes in Table 1 and the Table 2 algorithm-level averages for target suppression, collateral suppression, and validation change.

untested.parts: Resistance to simple recovery attacks; knowledge-level accuracy near chance (the study measures verbatim extraction probability only).
All; no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All; no direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
All; no rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context recovery.
All; no method claimed robust to attacks.

missing.what: Per-model RMU forget/retain under EA (Qwen3-8B F=24.5%, R=25.7%; Olmo-3-7B F=79.0%), which the average row r55 hides

record.verdict_notes: Retain-pool rows are linked to A's preservation clause; their state describes whether preservation holds, not whether suppression occurred. The measure is verbatim extraction probability (pz≥0.001), not knowledge accuracy, so 'near chance' maps only loosely. Olmo-3-7B uses |Wf|=38. EA uses evaluation windows directly and is a diagnostic, not a practical curator. Table 3/7 results (e.g., RMU with BM25-mid on Llama: F 94.3%, validation -45.5 pp) are declared in rows_left_out but are important for A's preservation clause. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures targeted extraction suppression and capability/retention changes, but does not establish near-chance performance in an attack setting or test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
The paper does not test a method as resistant to the recovery attacks in the claim.

tranche.reason: New setting: verbatim extraction of songs and books, curated forget sets, and a probabilistic-extraction measure. It has results on whether unlearning suppresses the target while preserving other content and general benchmarks. It does not use the original method or measure, so T3 fits rather than T2.

source_check.notes: Olmo-3-7B has a 38-work forget pool (Table 4 caption, Table 8 footnote), so the three-model means (r49-r55) mix pools of 50 and 38 despite the |Wf|=50 caption. EA uses the evaluation windows directly and is a robustness test, not a practical curator. Retain-pool extractability measures collateral suppression of other works, not general capability. The measure is verbatim extraction, not knowledge accuracy. Table 7 per-model cross-evaluation results (e.g. UNDIAL on BM25-pre: 96.7-100% forget, 79.0-91.8% retain loss) are not captured as rows.
